title.narrative: Reducing HIV infections and HIV related mortality among Somalis

description.narrative: Somalia - HIV - United Nations Children's Fund - UNICEF. This program has the following goals: By the end of 2028, the HIV prevalence rate in the general population of the country remains at less than 0.1%. By the end of 2028, the HIV prevalence rate among key and vulnerable populations (vulnerable women (FSWs), People Who Inject Drugs (PWID), people in uniform, truck drivers, and port workers) is reduced by 20% compared to the baseline data in 2023. By the end of 2028, the vertical HIV transmission rate from mother to children is less than 5%.. By the end of 2028, AIDS-related deaths among PLHIVs is reduced by 20% compared to the baseline data in 2023.. The objectives of this program are: By the end of 2028, at least 30% of people aged 15 to 49 will be able to correctly identify HIV prevention methods and reject important misconceptions about HIV transmission (as per the composite index of UNAIDS).. By the end of 2028, HIV transmission through blood transfusions is (remains at) 0%.. By the end of 2028, the percentage of key and vulnerable populations (vulnerable women (FSWs), People Who Inject Drugs (PWID), people in uniform, truck drivers, and port workers) who can correctly identify HIV prevention methods and reject important misconceptions about HIV transmission will increase by 30% compared to the baseline data. By the end of 2028, the key and vulnerable populations (vulnerable women (FSWs), People Who Inject Drugs (PWID), people in uniform, truck drivers, and port workers) who have used a condom in their latest high risk sexual contact will increase by 20% compared to the baseline 2023 data.. By the end of 2024, at least 30% of People Who Inject Drugs (PWID) use sterile and non-shared devices in their last injection.. By the end of 2028, an estimated 90% of pregnant women living with HIV have been covered by standard PMTCT treatment.. By the end of 2028, at least 95% of the estimated number of PLHIVs have been identified.. By the end of 2028, at least 95% of people diagnosed with HIV should receive ART.. By the end of 2028, at least 95% of people are on ART would have a viral load of less than 1,000.
